scenes.topic_description:
Situation: The interview has just started in the recruiter's office or online. You are applying for a manager position and need to introduce yourself clearly, understand how the interview will work, and hear what the company expects early in the role before deeper questions begin.
Learner: Candidate. Partner: Recruiter.
Not in this scene: detailed achievements, management examples, salary, benefits, next steps after the decision.
must_say: give your name — slot: the full name
say which position you are interviewing for — slot: the position
say where you worked before — slot: the workplace
say how long you worked there — slot: the length of time
explain your main area of work — slot: the area
ask what the interview process includes — slot: none
ask what this role focuses on first — slot: the time period
confirm you are ready to continue — slot: none
must_understand: asks you to introduce yourself and your background
asks which role you are applying for
asks where you worked and for how long
explains the interview stages
says what the role focuses on at the beginning

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: This is the main part of the interview with the hiring manager. Your fit for the manager role is being assessed through your experience, results, and leadership style. Your concern about salary belongs here because this is where expectations, evaluation, and compensation are usually discussed and understood.
Learner: Candidate. Partner: Hiring Manager.
Not in this scene: self-introduction, interview format, scheduling later rounds, accepting an offer, onboarding details.
must_say: explain your current responsibilities — slot: the responsibilities
say what results you achieved — slot: the result
explain how you manage people or projects — slot: the method
answer whether you have experience with something — slot: the area of experience
ask what success in this role looks like — slot: the time period
ask how performance is evaluated — slot: the area
ask what salary range is planned — slot: the role
ask whether the package includes a benefit — slot: the benefit
must_understand: asks about your current responsibilities and achievements
asks how you manage a team, projects, or priorities
asks whether you have experience in a specific area
says what results the company expects in the role
explains the salary range or what the package includes

scenes.topic_description:
Situation: The interview is ending, and you need practical information about what happens next. This interaction matters because a clear closing helps you follow the process professionally, stay available, and know whether anything else is required after the meeting.
Learner: Candidate. Partner: Recruiter.
Not in this scene: introducing yourself, discussing past experience in detail, salary negotiation, benefits discussion.
must_say: ask when you can expect feedback — slot: the time expression
ask whether there will be another interview stage — slot: the stage
ask who to contact with a question — slot: the topic
say you are still interested in the role — slot: the role
confirm your availability for the next step — slot: the time period
ask whether any documents are needed — slot: the document
ask what the next step is — slot: none
thank the partner for their time — slot: none
must_understand: says when you should expect an update
explains whether there is another stage
tells you who to contact with questions
asks about your availability for the next step
says whether any additional documents are needed
